audits.mathematicalReason: The shared border strips give the large square side length L = 24s + 25d, not 24s + 48d. The shaded-area condition is 576s²/L² = 0.64. Taking the positive square root, since lengths are positive, gives 24s/L = 0.8, hence L = 30s. Thus 25d = 6s and d/s = 6/25. Square-area calculation and equation modeling are directly assessed; square roots and percentage conversion support this solution.

figureEvidence.fact: The displayed 3-by-3 array has two interior gaps and two exterior margins across each row. The border width specified in the stem therefore occurs four times for three tiles, generalizing to n+1 border widths for n tiles.

audits.mathematicalReason: Because F lies on AD, angle FDC is 90°. The specified half-plane places DE on the exterior side shown, so angle FDE = 360° − 90° − 110° = 160°. Since DE = DF, triangle DFE has equal base angles, each (180° − 160°)/2 = 10°. Rays FA and FD are opposite, so angle AFE = 180° − 10° = 170°. The isosceles-triangle and adjacent-supplementary-angle scopes directly match the reasoning, with the listed angle and square properties providing support.

figureEvidence.fact: A, F, and D are collinear with F between A and D; CD meets AD at the square's corner D. The marked 110° angle is between DC and DE, and E is on the opposite side of line CD from A.

audits.mathematicalReason: The sector arc has length (3/4)(2π·4) = 6π inches. When the radii are joined, this arc becomes the cone's base circumference, so 2πr = 6π and r = 3 inches. The sector radius becomes slant height 4 inches, giving the positive cone height h = √(4² − 3²) = √7 inches. Consequently V = (1/3)πr²h = 3π√7 cubic inches. The cone-net correspondence is explicitly within cnm_258's criteria even though no surface-area calculation is needed; cone volume is the other direct target.

audits.mathematicalReason: There are two disjoint cases. On the top layer, each of the four top edges contributes 4−2 = 2 noncorner cubes with icing on exactly two faces, for 8 cubes. Below the top layer, each of the four vertical corner columns contributes three cubes, for 12 more. These include the bottom corner cubes because the bottom is uniced. The top corner cubes have three iced faces and are excluded. Thus the total is 4·2 + 4·3 = 20. This directly uses combined addition and multiplication counting, supported by cube face-and-edge structure.

audits.mathematicalReason: Label the top regions L and R and the bottom regions X, M, and Y from left to right. M touches all four other regions. After choosing M's color in 5 ways, choose L's in 4 ways and R's in 3 ways, since R touches both M and L. Then X has 3 choices excluding the colors of M and L, and Y has 3 choices excluding those of M and R. Hence there are 5·4·3·3·3 = 540 colorings. This enforces exactly the displayed adjacency restrictions while allowing nonadjacent regions to reuse colors, matching the assessed coloring scope and supporting multiplication principle.

figureEvidence.fact: The rectangle has two top regions and three bottom regions. The bottom-middle region shares a boundary with all four others; the additional adjacencies are top-left/top-right, top-left/bottom-left, and top-right/bottom-right. The staggered dividers create no additional contacts between nonadjacent pairs.

audits.mathematicalReason: Place the common center at O = (0,0) and the unrotated square at −3 ≤ x,y ≤ 3. Take its corner P = (3,3). The adjacent reentrant boundary vertex Q lies where x = 3 meets the rotated side x + √3y = 6, whose equation follows from 30°–60°–90° geometry. Thus Q = (3,√3). Joining O to all boundary vertices gives 24 congruent triangles, with consecutive triangles being mirror images. Each has boundary base 3−√3 and perpendicular height 3, so the total area is 24·3(3−√3)/2 = 108−36√3. Therefore a+b+c = 108+36+3 = 147, with c = 3 squarefree. Composite-area decomposition and rotation properties are defensible direct targets; the listed special-triangle, Pythagorean, triangle-area, and radical skills support this method.

Its boundary alternates exposed square corners and reentrant side intersections.

Its intersection with x = 3 is Q = (3,√3), using the special-angle values. Rotational and reflection symmetry make the 24 triangles obtained by joining the center to consecutive boundary vertices congruent. Each has base PQ = 3−√3 and height 3, so the area is 24·(1/2)·3(3−√3) = 108−36√3. Thus a+b+c = 147. Composite area is a valid assessed scope, square properties provide support, and the stated rotation/special-angle/triangle-area route is valid without being universally required.

The original sector radius is the cone's slant height, so its positive vertical height is √(16−9) = √7 inches. The volume is therefore (1/3)π·9·√7 = 3π√7 cubic inches. The assessed scopes correctly capture the sector-to-cone correspondence and volume calculation; arc length, circumference, and the Pythagorean theorem support them.
